Sword Art Online

Genres: Adventure, Drama, Fantasy, Romance, Science Fiction

Episode Count: S1: 25, S2: 24

Studio: A-1 Pictures

Director: Tomohiko Ito

Music: Yuki Kajura

Air Time: S1: July 7, 2012 – December 22, 2012, S2: July 5, 2014 - December 20, 2014

Additional Materials: Movie (2015), Sequel

The players of a virtual reality MMORPG, Sword Art Online, are trapped and fighting for their very lives. After it is announced that the only way to leave the game is by beating it, Kirito—a very powerful swordsman—and his friends take on a quest to free all the minds trapped in Aincrad. (Quick info from: Anime News Network )

Why was it hyped up?

Sword Art Online (SAO) was hyped up due to its premise of 'being trapped inside a video game' as well as its impressive production value.

Questions

General Series Questions

  • Is the hype justified for when the series aired? Is the hype still relevant?
  • Did you think the series was good?
  • If you have seen the anime, did hype for the series enhance or detract from your viewing experience?

Series Specific Questions

  • What did you think about the pacing of romance in the series?
  • How balanced do you think the powers are in SAO? Does this add or take away from the series?
  • Do you think interactions between characters in general is natural? Does this add or take away from the series?
  • Do you think the reactions by characters and then the game's 'society' overall to being trapped in a video game were portrayed convincingly? Remember to tag your spoilers! If in doubt, tag it anyway.

what did you think of the pacing of romance in the series?

I feel that the pacing of romance in the show between Kirito and Asuna was mostly fine. The only criticism I have of it is that the episode where they fight the first floor boss (episode 3 or something?) is almost never brought up again. It’s as if Kirito and Asuna never met before they both started fighting on the front lines in some ways. Obviously that first time they partied up has a big affect on Asuna, as she goes from “i didn't come to this town to eat good food” to maxing out her cooking skill. The show still shows the effects of that first meeting but I just wish that it was brought up more.

How balanced do you think the powers are in SAO? Does this add or take away from the series?

I don’t think Kirito is OP. The only thing he has that sets himself apart is the dual wielding thing, and that's just because Kirito has the highest reaction time of anybody in the game. Its shown pretty clearly in the show that Kirito is a no-life shut in, and to think that he would be high leveled in a MMO really isn’t unrealistic. I think Kirito only solos like two bosses in the show? The only one he really solos is Nicholas the Renegade, which is doable. There are a lot of strats in mmos to pull this off, mostly by just dodging a lot and slowly taking down something's health. The other one is the boss that the army rushes in to, and then while Kirito does most of the work he's backed up by Asuna and Klein. So Kiritos power level seems legit and makes sense to me. There are parts where it got out of hand though (see the final episode of the Aincrad arc.)

Do you think interactions between characters in general is natural? Does this add or take away from the series?

Yes. Everyone always complains about how Kirito has a harem but he totally doesn’t. People also complain about characters being attracted to Kirito for no real reason, but all the characters in the show (of which there aren’t even that many) that come on to Kirito have legit reasons for it. Sachi: her guild wants to put her on the front lines and in the vanguard which she isn't cool with, and Kirito pretty much says he’ll defend her so she won’t have to take on that role that she obviously has a problem with. Lisbeth: Seems to pretty much be alone most of the time in her shop and just wants somebody to love, and while she's in the middle of this emotional dilemma Kirito shows up. Silica: That relationship is just a big brother - little sister thing. Kirito felt bad because he was a dick to Sugu and now he may never see her again, and Silica was an only child I think? Probably just wanted to know what that was like. Also Kirito is a guy that's not creepy towards her so thats a plus. A major point here is that Kirito is never romantically interested in any of these girls (with the exception of Sachi probably). Even in ALO he never shows any sign of wanting to get with any of these girls since he has Asuna. Kirito is staunchly loyal.

Do you think the reactions by characters and then the game's 'society' overall to being trapped in a video game were portrayed convincingly?

Yeah for the most part. Everyone is freaked out at the beginning, the show shows people killing themselves all the time, some people use it as an opportunity to be the psychos that they really are (Laughing Coffin, Grimlock.) After being in the game for 2 years I think a lot of people would end up like the village fisherman, just accepting of the world they're in now as reality.

He can solo bosses, which no one else can (if other people was shown doing that using strategy, then I wouldn't mind the strategy excuse. Also, I don't remember if he actually used strategy to win, but I don't think so), he has the highest reaction time of all the players, he gets a special power because plot says so, and the only thing/player in the game that stands a chance against him is through cheating. How is this not OP?

You basically explained why it's a harem yourself. It doesn't matter if he's romantically interested in them or not, it's the girls romantic interest in him that matters. Besides, the main complaint about the harem is that it's a useless timesink (which it is), not that Kirito is unfaithful to Asuna.

Tbh we have no idea what he used to beat Nicholas The Renegade, that fight isn't even shown. I wish it was though because I thought the boss looked really cool.

Yes we never see that strategy in-game in SAO, but it's just a typical MMO/fighting game strat I used as an example. (roll/doge in a circle while the boss tries to attack you, attack them while doing so.) The dual wielding thing would have worked a lot better if it was a reward for maxing your swordsmanship skill or something, not just a secret one granted to Kirito.

I do think the show skews how op Kirito is though. 90% the zones that the show shows Kirito in he is easily a good 20 levels above the typical level of the zone. I remember reading or seeing somewhere (I think it was in SA Offline) that to beat a floor boss you need to be 10 levels above the floor number (lvl 20 to beat floor 10 boss for example.) Most of the shows subplots take place on floors 20-50ish, all places that Kirito will appear OP as shit because his level is so much higher than the standard for that floor. Great example is the scene where that PK guild tries to jump him and silica and they can barely even damage him.

We don't see Kirito 1v1 anyone of importance/equal footing besides the games creator either, so to judge his standing based off one opponent is kind of unfair. (The only other person he duels is asuna's bodyguard but that guy is like 10 levels below Kirito i think.)

The harem thing is just me misunderstanding the definition of harem, sorry about that. I assumed that for a harem to be a harem MC had to be interested in all the girls. As for it being a timesink, I can get that. I liked the Silica episode but nothing of overall importance happens, at least the Lisbeth episode gets the 2nd sword.

Right, I wasn't sure which one it was so was expecting it was part of the show.

And alright.

Didn't he 1v1 the poison dude? And didn't he 1v1 people in the fairy thingy? I don't really remember at this point.

And to be fair, what matters isn't purely how strong Kirito's statblock is, but how his character is handled in the show in regards to his power level. It doesn't matter that he doesn't face people his own level (which doesn't seem to exist anyways) because even if he did, he'd beat them regardless. The show is empowerment fantasy, Kirito gets a lot of things simply for being the protagonist, and he wouldn't lose, not because his statblock is high but because the writer wouldn't make a situation where he would lose. because plot allows him to do anything he want in order not to lose. And because of his ridiculous plot armor, the show lacks tension when you realize the show would do practically anything in order to make sure Kirito doesn't achieve a (meaningful) loss.

General Series Questions

Is the hype justified for when the series aired? Is the hype still relevant?

I actually wasn't watching anything at the time SAO started, (the Fairy Arc had already started when I discovered it) so it's initial hype was something I missed entirely. (Had two months away from reality ya see)

Anywho, as for now, definitely not. I just don't understand why so many want to put it on some pedestal when it was simply alright for what it was (especially after that second arc Shudder)

Did you think the series was good?

It's decent, some people will completely trash it, but I think it has it's moments. Particularly the fight scenes are very enjoyable, and the initial exploration both SAO and GGO were great to me, as it was like starting a new game. It breathed a bit of fresh air into a genre that only .hack had ever truly explored. It's a great gateway for someone who hasn't been exposed to many anime, but it's a pass if you've been watching anime for a while I feel like.

If you have seen the anime, did hype for the series enhance or detract from your viewing experience?

No, as mentioned earlier, the hype was non-existent to me. I only knew one person who liked it and that was my roommate at the time who was the one who showed it to me.

Series Specific Questions

What did you think about the pacing of romance in the series?

Terrible. Some might bring up how Asuna and Kirito knew each other for far longer than we were shown due to time skips, but that's no excuse for a romance to be rushed through like it was. I felt like they barely knew each other up to this point, so it just felt rushed to me, a bit out of nowhere. Maybe they felt it was okay in-game, but even the first time I watched it bugged me.

How balanced do you think the powers are in SAO? Does this add or take away from the series?

I do think that Kirito himself is pictured as a very powerful character. Based on a lot of the situations he gets in, particularly early on, due to being several levels higher than most of the characters he runs into. Then ALO and beyond happen, and I think they decided to just make him super strong. No one should just be great at any game they play from the start. That just gets ridiculous to me. I don't mind strong characters myself, so it wasn't a major detraction for me though.

Do you think interactions between characters in general is natural? Does this add or take away from the series?

Some of it is done pretty well. Aside from the harem aspect, a lot of the characters seem just like any other group of friends hanging out playing a game. As for the most part, the majority of people aren't going through hacking their way to the finish. They're leveling up at a normal pace, and just trying to survive in the world as best they can.

Do you think the reactions by characters and then the game's 'society' overall to being trapped in a video game were portrayed convincingly?

To an extent. I do think after months of being trapped, that you would simply try to adapt to your new life. Humans are about survival, and you might as well keep on working towards something while you're stuck. Murderers and bad people still exist, as such good people still exist. It becomes their lives, but they still plan to leave. It's the one thing I think that it has over Log Horizon, in that, the characters are actively trying to leave SAO. Which is probably the most realistic thing about it all.

The Old Course at St. Andrews opened in 1552, though the sport was first played on the Links at St Andrews in the early 1400s, making the Old Course one of the three oldest courses in the world and the "home of golf." Today it hosts perhaps the most recognizable European golf tournament: The Open.

One of the unique features of the Old Course are the large double greens. The Swilcan Bridge, spanning the first and 18th holes, has become a famous icon for golf in the world. Everyone who plays the 18th hole walks over this 700 year old bridge, and many iconic pictures of the farewells of the most iconic golfers in history have been taken on this bridge. A replica of it has been built in St. Augustine, FL.

Along with that, the Old Course has 112 bunkers which are all individually named and have their own unique story and history behind them. The two most famous are the 10 ft deep "Hell Bunker" on the 14th hole, and the "Road Bunker" on the 17th hole. Countless professional golfers have seen their dreams of winning the Open Championship squandered by hitting their balls in those bunkers.

It's worth noting that no player from any country represented at the Summit has ever won an Open Championship at the Old Course, so regardless of who wins and the caliber of world leaders competing against one another, history will be made here today.

Since many state leaders have chosen to remain in their hotel rooms during social hours, the turnout for the golf tournament is rather modest for an event at the Old Course.
